rites.text: Lalia is the concept of the wall-bound tradition of Elaennirlys, a set of vows and sung boundaries that kept the holding cities from the wild in the Walled Age. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall split the old compacts, the concept was tested and reshaped as orders and first crossings challenged its meaning.

rites.name: Thothun
rites.text: Thothun is a concept of Elaennirlys, an arcane principle of binding and unbinding that shaped the walls and orders of the Walled Age. It was the idea that a boundary could hold a sea or a sky in place, and that the same boundary could be broken by a single deliberate word. Its influence was most visible during the Age of Sundering, when landfall split old bonds between peoples.

rites.name: Ukamauta
rites.text: Ukamauta is the concept of a binding oath sworn over stone, held by the orders that tended the walls of Elaennirlys through the Walled Age. When landfall broke the old bonds in the Age of Sundering, the concept was split between the orders that kept their vows and the crossers who claimed its meaning for themselves.

rites.name: Ukatamoma
rites.text: Ukatamoma is the concept of a sealing word spoken to hold back the drifting dark between the walled cities of Elaennirlys. In the Age of Sundering it was taken as the grounds for the first crossings, when orders broke their old bonds and sent ships into the unwalled deep.

rites.name: Ceriallor
rites.text: A bound power that works only on one particular handheld console. It belongs to a later world of machines and is limited to that single device.

rites.name: Cistium
rites.text: A passive ability that quietly taints the surroundings of its bearer. It arrived alongside a newer system of chosen champions, granting them a lingering corrupting touch.

rites.name: Tolum
rites.text: A passive discipline that gives a fighter steadier aim during strikes. It was introduced alongside the champion system during a later revision of the realm's rules.

rites.name: Cestium
rites.text: A furious finishing technique that a fighter unleashes in a single decisive blow. It was introduced into the combat arts through a later revision of the training manuals.

rites.name: Veores
rites.text: A protective craft that a supporter learns once their skill reaches a high standing. It is used during allied conflicts to shield companions from harm.

rites.name: Seraurnium Nontor
rites.text: A passive craft that rests quietly within a champion's system and activates on its own. It was added to the champion framework during a later revision.

rites.name: Oriarnus Serisanum
rites.text: A bonded couple may unravel their shared band to gain a lasting blessing that makes healing magic cheaper to cast. The blessing grows stronger with experience and cannot be fixed onto any worn gear.

rites.name: Orarium Corestillus
rites.text: A lasting enhancement that a skill or power grants to its user for a time. It is shaped by a newer system of rewards and judgments.

rites.name: Vilesus
rites.text: A card from the Mirrorvale Assembly set that lets its holder dodge an imminent threat. It acts as a quick, last-moment action.

rites.name: Telentarnum
rites.text: A bought training regimen that quickens a rider's steed through a set of single-use draughts. It has no daily cap and needs at least one steed, and it stops working once the steed reaches a certain tier.

rites.name: Sillor Amiantor
rites.text: A quiet passive craft that appears within a certain realm and was added to the world alongside a new system of champions. It is a built-in trait rather than something a character actively performs.

rites.name: Nolor Mantaunor
rites.text: A quiet passive talent that a champion carries within their stance. It emerges from a structured system of champions introduced in a later renewal of the realm.

rites.name: Serestium
rites.text: A devastating ultimate technique drawn from the mastery of raw elemental force. It was introduced into the practice of arms only in a recent revision of the codex.

rites.name: Orialor Ninor
rites.text: A devastating ultimate technique of combat that a warrior unleashes by channeling raw elemental fury through their weapon. It was introduced in a later revision of the training manuals.

rites.name: Teorantium
rites.text: A learned skill-craft that a practitioner gains through training. It sharpens how well they perform particular tasks over time.

rites.name: Sereosia Seraullinor
rites.text: A quiet, passive knack that surfaces within a certain order of wardens once a newer system of champions is adopted. It has no active form and simply lingers in the background of a fighter's craft.

rites.name: Miantalia
rites.text: A passive discipline practiced by a warrior order, quietly strengthening its wielder over time. It belongs to a sequence of related techniques tied to the dawn.

rites.name: Orillaranum Seorneres
rites.text: A quiet inborn talent that lets a combatant sense what lies ahead. It arrived alongside the rise of formal champion-bearers and works without any conscious effort.

rites.name: Valesia Riallus
rites.text: A card-borne power that allows its bearer to unleash devastating forces of ruin. It belongs to a later collection of cards in its world.

rites.name: Valirnum Nesteoranum
rites.text: A passive craft that is introduced alongside a newer system of champions. Its effect is quietly carried by the bearer without needing to be called upon.

rites.name: Miasanum Seralus
rites.text: A brief, drifting trick that a traveler can invoke to slip past a foe's notice for a moment. It belongs to a later collection of added tools.

rites.name: Valilor
rites.text: A holder may seize a nearby thing and shift it across the space around them without placing it in their pack. The grip holds the item at the same distance it had when first taken, and bumping it against a surface can shorten that distance.

rites.name: Reolor
rites.text: A passive endurance quality that is always active within a fighter's training. It was added to the trial system when the champion rankings were introduced.

rites.name: Tiria Telaseornes
rites.text: A soldier who lifts the spirits of nearby comrades in the field. Its presence steadies allies and encourages them to press on through danger.

rites.name: Villium
rites.text: A quiet passive craft that takes hold within a bearer without any active call. It arrived alongside a newer system of chosen champions.

rites.name: Valaustolia
rites.text: A quiet passive gift that the bearer carries without effort. It arrived alongside a new system of champions, and it stirs the mind toward fresh ideas.

rites.name: Sianeolus
rites.text: A passive craft that a warrior carries, granting a steady surge of vigor during combat. It was added alongside a newer system for raising fighters into champions.

rites.name: Cesanum Nernus
rites.text: A passive technique that quietly activates within a warrior's training. It first took shape when a new ranking system for champions was adopted.

rites.name: Telirus Meosor
rites.text: A parting rule that triggers when a bearer is cast down, letting its final moment unleash a set effect. Such effects may return a chosen token to the holder's grasp, strike a foe, or call forth a new ally.

rites.name: Teleranum Valianor
rites.text: A closing blow that a fighter can deliver with a dramatic, filmed flourish to finish off an opponent. It can be used against nearly any foe, and foes can use it against the warrior as well.

rites.name: Telaunilium
rites.text: A fighter's advanced skill for wielding two blades at once, unlocked after long practice. It lets the wielder strike with both weapons in a flurry.

rites.name: Amintaunus
rites.text: A grand technique that a wielder can unleash in combat once their weapon mastery has reached its peak. It appeared with a later revision of the realm's martial rules.

rites.name: Veorastanum
rites.text: A passive gift of aid drawn from arcane reserves, belonging to a support discipline. It becomes accessible to practitioners who reach the third tier of that discipline.

rites.name: Nisteonia
rites.text: A modern ultimate technique that channels radiant energy through a warrior's weapon. It was introduced in a later revision of the system.

rites.name: Veornia Seresor
rites.text: A quiet, always-on talent that a warrior carries without effort. It was recognized as a formal ability once the ranking system of combat champions was established.

rites.name: Collanum Cistium
rites.text: A zealous guardian's ultimate technique, drawn from a dawn-bound discipline of wrathful light. It stands among the strongest skills of its path.

rites.name: Causelanum
rites.text: A gesture that a wanderer can perform to show off their strength. It is sold by a merchant house that trades in ornaments and rare goods.

rites.name: Corintium Oreorines
rites.text: A devastating finishing technique that a wielder unleashes in a single overwhelming assault. It was introduced in a later revision of the realm's combat codex.

rites.name: Oreoria Rintalles
rites.text: A quiet, always-on talent that appears within a certain realm. It arrived alongside a newer ranking-and-champion arrangement introduced in a later revision of the world's rules.

rites.name: Miantinor
rites.text: A passive art that quietly activates within a warrior's practice. It arrived alongside a newer system for organizing champions and their abilities.

rites.name: Sanium Veostium
rites.text: A passive craft that appears in a certain arena of the world. It was introduced alongside the Champion System during a later revision of the rules.

rites.name: Orontus Oronaurnia
rites.text: A quiet trait that stirs whenever a creature carrying it strikes the opposing side, awakening a hidden effect in that moment.

rites.name: Mantia Orianum
rites.text: A high-tier technique for fighters who wield a weapon in each hand, serving as the first refinement of a deep-cutting strike. It is one of the advanced variations open to practitioners of that style.

rites.name: Meolinia
rites.text: A passive talent that is always active and quietly strengthens its bearer against harm. It was added alongside a newer system for shaping champions.

rites.name: Telaroses
rites.text: A passive craft that operates quietly in the background of a warrior's training. It was added alongside a newer system for choosing and advancing champions.

rites.name: Lesor Miastaullus
rites.text: A minor enchanted effect that is part of a bonus add-on package offered for survival-style play. It is a magical craft drawn into the optional content layer of the realm.

rites.name: Seolantus
rites.text: A tactical maneuver in which a striking action is repeated in a rolling wave, letting its force echo onward into a further blow when played as part of a larger set.

rites.name: Vellia Amollus
rites.text: A quick evasive leap that lets a fighter slip past blows and shake off restraining effects. Repeated leaps in quick succession drain more of the body's endurance each time.

rites.name: Centeollor
rites.text: A passive discipline that a bearer carries without effort, granting steady endurance against harm. It was taught to warriors as part of a newer system of renowned champions.

rites.name: Sausalanum
rites.text: A passive art that arrives alongside a newly introduced champion arrangement. Its nature belongs to the broader scheme of combat that the arrangement brings in.

rites.name: Valauranum Naurnes
rites.text: Charged rifts open late in a duel with a guardian machine, draining one fighter's strength before releasing a final surge. The surge cannot be broken once it begins.

rites.name: Coriarillum
rites.text: A dormant trigger that wakes whenever a bearer's creature brings down another creature. Its effect is set off at that moment of destruction.

rites.name: Leneolor
rites.text: A quiet technique that lets a practitioner vanish from sight. When paired with a dark consuming art, it can also make the user turn invisible.

rites.name: Veolor Nauntor
rites.text: A quiet, constant talent that a champion carries within their own training. It was added alongside a newer system for raising warriors, and it works without being called upon.

rites.name: Serellanum Oristenor
rites.text: A swift action token that nullifies a spell cast by an opponent. It is drawn from a supplementary bundle added later to the set.

rites.name: Oraurnia Castiarum
rites.text: A quiet, constant talent that sharpens how exactly a caster's workings strike their intended mark. It came into being alongside a newer system for naming chosen champions.

rites.name: Valiasium Amesilum
rites.text: A sorcerer's final art that draws a dark working into a zone and holds it there, dampening the magic of everything caught inside. It belongs to a practitioner's sinister branch of arcane craft.

rites.name: Linolus
rites.text: A quiet inner discipline that lets a bearer endure hardship and refuse to yield. It arrived as part of a recently formed ranking of champions.

rites.name: Ciarnostus
rites.text: A dimming effect that lowers the chance a caster lands a sharp, potent strike when working magic. It stands opposite to an effect that sharpens such surges.

rites.name: Orasia Colleosum
rites.text: A passive talent that quietly operates within a wider system, introduced alongside a champion-selection framework during a major later revision.

rites.name: Sianostia
rites.text: A mechanic that lets a wearer be pulled into an earlier era to relive a past struggle. Some relics can also carry a traveler back to a bygone moment, or send a sealed being forward across the ages.

rites.name: Viarnarium
rites.text: A set of mighty strikes that a fighter can awaken once a gathered reserve of focus fills completely. Each strike grows stronger through repeated practice and draws on a separate pool of charge rather than ordinary energy.

rites.name: Sastelia
rites.text: A deliberate stillness that lets a wanderer let hours slip by. It is used to wait for markets to open, to see a task through, to shift from dusk to dawn, or to restore one's strength and inner reserves.

rites.name: Roranum Telolum
rites.text: A passive ability that quietly lets a warrior ride into battle with a steadier stride. It was added alongside a newer system of champions that rewards dedicated fighters.

rites.name: Mielora
rites.text: Mielora is the woven discipline of the Elaennirlys arcane realm, a craft that bends the hidden currents of mentality into visible effects. Its practitioners trace their lineage to the old choir of the Lantern Seers, who first learned to sing the world into compliance. Although every born creature carries a trace of the craft, those raised among the high cliff-cities channel it with unmatched grace.

rites.name: Silaeralwen
rites.text: Silaeralwen is a dormant resonance of woven sigils that, when a caster kindles it, blankets a wide ring of ground with overlapping pulses of ash and frost. It binds to whoever speaks its name first, growing stronger with each crowd it sweeps clean.

rites.name: Veneillora
rites.text: Veneillora is a tuning-lattice of resonant glass that drinks the stored light of fallen stars and gives it back to whatever tool is bound to its core. Its keepers measure its strength in pulses, and each pulse can be channeled into a blade, a lens, or a hull until the glass runs dry.

rites.name: Ilyara
rites.text: Ilyara is a binding-rite of the Elaennirlys mystics, a sigil of self-ward that turns its bearer's own pulse into a shield and mend. Those who take it up learn to breathe a fraction of their vitality outward into a single sealed ring of protection. It is valued for its quiet, inward discipline rather than for reaching beyond the body.

rites.name: Eluarlys
rites.text: Eluarlys is a conceptual delivery mode in the Elaennirlys omniverse, where an arcane working is hurled across open air to strike a chosen mark rather than being laid on skin or kept within the caster. Its practitioners in the third age of the sixth epoch treat distance as a binding they must tie, and the greater the span they cross, the more of their own stored breath the working demands.

rites.name: Eliolinys
rites.text: Eliolinys is the close-contact art of the Elaennirlys arcane tradition, in which a caster's power is laid directly onto a surface, wound, or willing body rather than hurled across the air. Practitioners favor it for its precision, its economy of magicka, and its safety among allies in crowded battle. It is most often shaped into healing hands and sharp, focused wards.

rites.name: Eluamae
rites.text: Eluamae is a verdant witch-light woven from the Illusion weave of Elaennirlys, a glow that pools where a caster's attention settles and widens with their resolve. Apprentices practise it endlessly on their own skin, which trades safety in the dark for a learned clarity of mind.

rites.name: Silirelora
rites.text: Silirelora is a conceptual lattice of arcane pattern-threads woven through the Elaennirlys, a discipline that binds a practitioner's will into interlocking sigils. Its adepts gain mastery through repeated invocation and patient instruction, so each working refines the weave a little further. Stronger adepts can shape its threads into weapons, shelters, and restorative fields, but only through careful tending of the underlying pattern.

rites.name: Alaalora
rites.text: Alaalora is a restorative art of the Elaennirlys powers, practiced by quiet mender-scholars who tend wounds while others slumber. Its adepts can mend the flesh of a world's worth of sufferers in a single night's rest. Its mastery is said to hold back the slow decay of entire realms.

rites.name: Nuanora
rites.text: Nuanora is an ancient arcane current woven through Elaennirlys, a discipline of quiet sight that lets its practitioners perceive hidden threads of causation across the world. Scholars of the third age still debate whether it reveals futures or merely listens to the echoes of choices not yet made.

rites.name: Siluamae
rites.text: Siluamae is a quiet discipline of mending woven through the Arcane realm of Elaennirlys, practiced by hermit-weavers who knit broken bones, failing hearts, and spoiled blood back into health. Its practitioners also bind warding veils over the living and gently coax restless dead to drift away from the places they haunt.

rites.name: Nuinaeleth
rites.text: Nuinaeleth is a concept of the Arcane realm in the Elaennirlys omniverse, a faculty of guiding one's will along an unseen line toward a chosen mark. Practitioners of the third age learn to bend projectile arcs, warp the distance between striker and quarry, and make wounds find their target even through intervening walls. Its mastery is said to separate the merely clever from the truly inevitable.

rites.name: Lyariel
rites.text: Lyariel is the name given to the discipline of weaving harmful intent into threads of ambient arcane light, so that a single strand can sear flesh or unravel armor. Practitioners of the Elaennirlys tradition in the third age of the E6 era train their hands to pull these threads taut before a blow lands. Its power is shaped by the wielder's will rather than by raw strength.

rites.name: Alaema
rites.text: Alaema is an arcane concept in the Elaennirlys omniverse, a lens of resonance that governs how far a living will can project before it frays. Its power scales with how deeply the wielder draws it back, so the faintest tug reaches a hand's breadth while a full draw can span a valley. Practitioners of the E6 age treat it as a measure of intent rather than distance.

rites.name: Alaanwen
rites.text: Alaanwen is a quiet rite of the Vessel-Choirs, in which a combatant lowers a shining ward and speaks a hushed plea that stills an opponent's hand. It works only on those who already hold kindness toward the caster, and fails against beasts, wardens of the deep, or spirits bound to fixed oaths.

rites.name: Silenys
rites.text: Silenys was an ambush-spell woven into a mountain pass, a sudden rupture of sorcerous tension that a waiting host could unleash at a single signal. Its arcane charge was set to burst outward over the whole valley at once. It was the moment a deceived invading army discovered it had marched into a trap.

rites.name: Amorneontes
rites.text: A draining cry of ancient winged beings that siphons the life force from those nearby. It is used by the mightiest of the great sky-serpents.

rites.name: Vhaigok
rites.text: Vhaigok is the concept of a branching ending in Elaennirlys, a bent thread of possibility that the Library of the Three Futures shelves beside every other outcome. It is not an agent but a standing rule that keeps unrealized endings from collapsing into the present.
